A TEAM WITH BOUNDARIES

Let your agents do real work.
Keep the keys and the final say.

Credentials, scope and decisions. Each in its place.

01

Access without the keys

Cells hold placeholders only. A trusted proxy injects or re-signs GitHub, AWS, Linear and model credentials on the way out; trusted services act for agents on Gmail, Drive, Notion and Slack.

CREDENTIALS STAY OUTSIDE
02

Each agent, only its own

Every agent has its own connectors, folders, skills and the agents it may delegate to, and optionally a list of hosts it may reach. Change them in a settings panel; nothing else is in reach.

SCOPED PER AGENT
03

The writes that matter wait for you

Merges, deletions, pushes to main and access changes always wait for your approval, whoever asked. Mark an agent's connector ask and all its writes there wait too, with the chain of how the task started.

YOUR FINAL SAY
04

A fresh cell for every task

Each task runs in a disposable cell inside a local VM, with no network but its own proxy. Before a cell is destroyed, it is scanned for real credential values.

ISOLATED AND CHECKED
05

A team, not a single bot

Describe an agent and the builder proposes it. Agents delegate to each other, start on a schedule or for new issues, and share skills you add from a folder or GitHub.

BUILD, DELEGATE, TRIGGER
06

Made for your terminal

A terminal UI and a CLI: chat with agents, follow their tasks, review held writes in full-screen dialogs. Every action is one leader key away, or in the command palette.

TUI AND CLI

Read the getting started guide ↗
  1. 01

    Install

    scripts/anchi setup install creates the VM, the trusted services and the base image. Unlock the vault once per VM start.

  2. 02

    Connect runtimes and accounts

    Import your Codex login or a Claude Code token, and connect the services your agents need. Secrets go straight to the VM vault.

  3. 03

    Build your team

    Describe an agent to the builder, review its proposal, and give it a task. Approve the writes it holds for you.

A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

Before you begin.

Read the security model ↗
Can I use Anchi today?+

Anchi is an open-source developer preview that runs from a checkout of its repository. It has not had a security audit and is not distributed as signed releases. macOS on Apple Silicon is supported; Linux is experimental. Follow the getting started guide to set it up.

Does credential isolation keep my data private?+

No. What an agent reads can reach the cloud model and any public host the agent may reach; an egress list narrows those hosts but cannot stop an allowed one from receiving data. Anchi keeps credentials out of agents' hands; it is not data isolation, and not suited to unattended work on sensitive real accounts.

What could a compromised agent still do?+

Use what it was given: the operations its connectors allow, the folders it was listed, the hosts it may reach. It cannot take a credential with it, reach another agent's resources, or get past the approvals that hold its writes.

Do I need to approve every action?+

No. Tool calls inside a cell run freely; the cell is the boundary. High-risk operations always wait for you, and other writes wait where you set an agent's connector to ask. Gmail, Drive, Notion and Slack can also be set to ask before every request of every agent.

Which agents and services are supported?+

Codex and Claude Code, with your subscriptions. GitHub, AWS and Linear through the proxy; Gmail (read-only), Google Drive, Notion and Slack through trusted services; folders under ~/AnchiWorkspaces on macOS. Validation with every real account is still in progress.
